newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker after losses pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker after losses pared.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker but with most of the day's losses pared as firm spreads helped the market recover from a dip following the larger-than-expected hike in LME stocks Friday, traders said.
The market was awaiting Monday's session, the first in a week of the extreme tightness on LME, with traders expecting the cash to a day to hit the limit still in effect.
LME backwardation remained firm, ending at $280/$290, just off the high of about $300, and still strong enough to underpin nearby prices, traders said.
March COMEX copper settled 0.45 cent lower at 106.65 cents a lb, traded 107.10 to 105.20. Spot January went out 0.30 cent weaker at 111.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 6,364 lots.
LME stocks on Friday rose 12,775 tonnes to 156,000 tonnes, with 4,525 tonnes of the hike in the U.S. as metal from COMEX moved into LME depots because of the stronger London premium.
LME cash premium is a wide 4.5 to 5 cents over spot COMEX, with early February LME dates up to the 19th, also at a premium over its New York counterpart, giving plenty of scope for arbitrage deals.

But surprisingly, some metal was still being loaded into COMEX's warehouse in Amarillo in recent days, a trader noted. With 20,184 short tons of COMEX metal still left at close of trade Thursday, more was set to flow into LME stockpiles in Long Beach and elsewhere over the coming two weeks.
"Almost everything that's deliverable will be coming out if this thing (tightness on LME) lasts until February, and it looks like it is," the trader said.
